evidence: host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt: when fn-owner-cat-may-seal answers nil (or FN_NATIVE_TEST_CAT_SEAL_REFUSE), PREPARED := :recovery-required; the refusal branch consumes the reservation (fn-owner-refuse-reservation :refused), unfences the store, then returns (fnn-owner-prepare-refusal-word :recovery-required). That case has arms for :duplicate :conflict :clock-unusable :refused :unaffordable :memberships :article-numbers-exhausted :canonical-size-unavailable :invalid-binding :invalid only; otherwise (fnn-fault ...) = fnn-store-fault, which fnn-owner-attempt-handlers re-signals after setting (fnn-store-fenced store) t. It escapes fnn-owner-drain-one and fnn-owner-commit-start-locked (whose handler-case names only fnn-store-indeterminate), so the committer (or the inline drain) faults the service.
fix: Give the gate's refusal its own ACL2-named outcome word (the try-later refusal the client can retry), decided by ACL2 per r71-F15's design (:outcomes in the entry's result) rather than a new host arm; until then do not route a refused-before-seal prepare through the fault arm. Then run tests.test_native_post_seal_gate on an image and extend it to assert the node still answers ARTICLE after both refusals.
scenario: Any POST while the index writer holds an unfinished ticket or a prepared catalog commit is pending (books/catalog-may-seal.lisp: the conditions the gate exists for), or the developer image under FN_NATIVE_TEST_CAT_SEAL_REFUSE=1 (tests/test_native_post_seal_gate.py): the first POST is answered by no reply and the owner exits 4 with the store fenced, though nothing was sealed and the reservation was consumed as a refusal. test_native_post_seal_gate expects TWO 'POST seal-gate refused' lines and a serving node; by this reading it sees one (the second client's connect error is swallowed by its except) and fails.
title: A POST the catalog's seal gate refuses stops the node: fnn-owner-prepare-refusal-word has no arm for :recovery-required, so the clean refusal becomes a fenced-store fault (exit 4)
